author: ʿAntara ibn Shaddād
claim: Horse struck by spears on its chest 'complains to me with tears and taḥamḥum'; al-Zawzanī glosses taḥamḥum as a broken sound that is not ṣahīl — direct lexical witness for the ḥamḥama / ṣahīl contrast in the ḍabḥ definition

author: Imruʾ al-Qays
claim: Horse 'jayyāsh' whose ihtizām (rumbling sound inside the chest) when its heat boils is like a boiling cauldron — sound of exertion from the chest; thematic-lexical parallel to ḍabḥ as breath forced out of the working chest (not the word ḍabḥ itself)

author: Imruʾ al-Qays
claim: Source of the lexicon's example: the hunting horse 'fa-ʿādā ʿidāʾan bayna thawrin wa-naʿjatin / dirākan wa-lam yunḍaḥ bi-māʾin fa-yughsali'; al-Zawzanī glosses ʿidāʾ as muwālāt, taking two quarries in one run

author: Imruʾ al-Qays
claim: Horse with 'the flanks of a gazelle, legs of an ostrich, the lope of a wolf and the taqrīb of a fox-cub' — attests taqrīb as a named gait, the reference point for ḍabḥ/ḍabʿ as 'a run above taqrīb'

author: Imruʾ al-Qays
claim: 'wa-qad aghtadī wa-l-ṭayru fī wukunātihā / bi-munjaridin qaydi l-awābidi haykali' — setting out at dawn on a racing horse before the birds leave their nests; thematic parallel for night run ending in a morning raid (not lexical ḍabḥ)

author: Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd
claim: 'wa-aṣfara maḍbūḥin naẓartu ḥiwārahu / ʿalā l-nāri wa-stawdaʿtuhu kaffa mujmidi' — a yellow maysir arrow-shaft 'maḍbūḥ' (scorched/straightened by fire); direct lexical witness for qidḥ maḍbūḥ; uncertain whether in al-Zawzanī's recension of the muʿallaqa or only in the dīwān

author: Salāma ibn Jandal
work: al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt (also al-Aṣmaʿiyyāt?), poem 'awdā l-shabābu ḥamīdan dhū l-taʿājībi'
claim: 'wa-l-ʿādiyātu asābiyyu l-dimāʾi bihā / ka-anna aʿnāqahā anṣābu tarjībi' — al-ʿādiyāt used for horses (raiding chargers) with streaks of blood on their necks; direct lexical witness for ʿādiya = khayl mughīra

author: Salāma ibn Jandal
claim: Horse description in the same poem: the neck rising to the head over a juʾjuʾ (breast) like a perfume-grinding stone dyed with blood — the horse's chest as focal image

author: al-Find al-Zimmānī (Shahl ibn Shaybān)
work: Dīwān al-Ḥamāsa, Bāb al-ḥamāsa, opening poem (al-Marzūqī, Sharḥ)
claim: 'wa-lam yabqa siwā l-ʿudwāni dinnāhum kamā dānū' — 'udwān' as open aggression answered in kind; parallels udvân = ẓulm ṣurāḥ and the measured reply of 2:194; al-Marzūqī glosses ʿudwān

author: Qurayṭ ibn Unayf al-ʿAnbarī
claim: Satire of a tribe that repays the wrong of wrongdoers with forgiveness — 'yajzūna min ẓulmi ahli l-ẓulmi maghfiratan' — thematic witness on whether answering transgression is praise or blame (thematic, not ʿ-d-w lexical)

author: Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā
claim: 'wa-man lā yadhud ʿan ḥawḍihi bi-silāḥihi / yuhaddam wa-man lā yaẓlimi l-nāsa yuẓlami' — transgression vs. defence; thematic parallel only for the ethics of crossing limits

author: unknown (Ḥamāsa nasīb or rithāʾ)
claim: Formula 'ʿadat-nī ʿawādin / ʿadatnī ʿan ziyāratiki l-ʿawādī' — preoccupations that turn one away from one's purpose; direct witness for ʿawādī / ʿādiya = shughl that diverts; attribution and location uncertain

author: various (marāthī)
claim: Elegies naming the ʿawādī / ʿādiyāt of time (dahr) that seize men; al-Marzūqī may gloss ʿawādī as ṣawārif/ʿawāʾiq

author: Dhū l-Iṣbaʿ al-ʿAdwānī
work: al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt (or Ḥamāsa), poem to his cousin ʿAmr
claim: 'yā ʿAmru illā tadaʿ shatmī wa-manqaṣatī / aḍribka ḥattā taqūla l-hāmatu sqūnī' — the hāma (owl-spirit) that cries out at night over the slain; context for 'al-hām taḍbaḥ' (thematic: hāma's cry, not ḍabḥ itself)

author: Tawba ibn al-Ḥumayyir
claim: 'law anna Laylā l-akhyaliyyata sallamat ... la-sallamtu taslīma l-bashāshati aw zaqā / ilayhā ṣadan min jānibi l-qabri ṣāʾiḥu' — the ṣadā crying from the grave; night-bird sound of the ṣadā listed with ḍabḥ in the lexicon (thematic)

author: unknown
claim: Any direct occurrence of the root ḍ-b-ḥ in horse, fox, owl or wolf contexts (ḍābiḥ, ḍawābiḥ, taḍbaḥu, ḍubāḥ); I do not recall a specific verse in these collections — lexical sweep only

author: ʿAntara ibn Shaddād (attributed)
work: Dīwān ʿAntara (not roster; may be quoted in a commentary)
claim: 'wa-l-khaylu taʿlamu ḥīna taḍbaḥu fī / ḥiyāḍi l-mawti ḍabḥā' — direct lexical witness for ḍabḥ of horses in battle, cited by tafsīr for 100:1; attribution uncertain, probably outside the roster

author: unknown
claim: Forms of ḍ-b-ʿ for the forward reach of forelegs (ḍabʿ, ḍawābiʿ, ḍabaʿat) in mount descriptions; uncertain, lexical sweep

author: unknown (horse descriptions, e.g. Abū Duʾād al-Iyādī, Ṭufayl al-Ghanawī)
claim: Horse-poets' use of ḥuḍr and ʿadw for the full gallop, and ʿadwān/ʿadawān as epithet of a good runner; uncertain specific verses

author: Labīd ibn Rabīʿa
claim: His mare driven hard 'until she grew hot and her bones lightened ... her neck/breast poured and her girth was wet with the foam of sweat' — exertion visible on the running horse's body (thematic, not ḍabḥ)

author: unknown
claim: Hooves striking sparks from flint (marw, ṣawwān) — imagery of 100:2 joined to ḍabḥ via maḍbūḥ flints; recall vague

author: unknown
claim: maḍbūḥ applied to stones or wood blackened by fire, and ḍabḥ as ashes / sun-darkened colour; possibly rajaz of al-ʿAjjāj or Ruʾba (outside roster) — sweep only

author: ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm
claim: 'taraknā l-khayla ʿākifatan ʿalayhi / muqalladatan aʿinnatahā ṣufūnā' — horses standing in ṣufūn (resting on three legs); direct witness for ṣāfināt of 38:31

author: unknown
claim: kanūd in poetry for one ungrateful of favours (kanūd li-l-niʿma); recall uncertain
